clue.text: They value animals carrying gold aboard

parts.note: asses are donkeys, so animals in the plural

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: aboard means on a ship, and SS (steamship) is the crossword ship
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Beasts of burden are hauling gold overseas, and someone is pricing the cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text reads 'abroad', an OCR swap; 'aboard' is the usual signal for going inside a ship, here the steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Assessors are officials who estimate worth, for tax or insurance, so they value things.

clue.text: Horse-man out East?

definitions.meaning: a breed of horse from the Middle East
a man from the Arab world, out in the East

explanation.definitionFit: Arabian names both a famous horse breed and a native of Arabia.

clue.text: One stone from pile of stones seen to collapse on Marines

parts.note: a cairn is a heap of stones built as a marker
to go is to give way, as a structure goes
RM stands for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A heap of rocks topples onto a squad of marines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just sets the Marines last; 'seen to' is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairngorm is smoky quartz from the Scottish mountains of that name, a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Financial agent's office? Is in favour of office in the church

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a curacy is the post held by a curate

explanation.surface: A clue asking which church post a financial agent might hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A procurator acts as an agent handling another's affairs, and his post is a procuracy.

clue.text: Gemstone taken from ring first placed in funeral fire

indicators.note: the ring and that letter are set within the fire

parts.note: a pyre is a pile burnt at a funeral
O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word placed is wanted

explanation.surface: A jewel taken off a ring is thrown onto a funeral pyre.
explanation.walkthrough: O and P, the first of 'placed', go between PYR and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyrope is a deep red garnet used as a gem.

clue.text: A camping disaster in a military operation

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things wrecked, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A camping trip goes wrong during army manoeuvres.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign is a connected series of military actions.

clue.text: Dish Rex is to turn to

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: turn tells us the first word to is read the other way round

explanation.surface: King Rex is about to turn to a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked in stock.

clue.text: A big rodent — but there may be a cat near!

indicators.note: says the letters of the words cat near may form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Beware a large rat: a cat may be close by.
explanation.definitionFit: The cane rat is a large African rodent found in grassland and reed beds.

clue.text: It's striped and seen to tear around in outer space

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit inside the sky

parts.note: the sky stands loosely for space above

indicators.note: tear around suggests careering wildly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A striped object is spotted hurtling about in space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen to' is padding; 'around' marks the anagram of the tearing word, and 'in' places it after the first letter of the space word.
explanation.definitionFit: Streaky means marked with streaks or stripes, as streaky bacon is.

clue.text: Thinking something seen on April first is funny

indicators.note: the opening letter of April is taken

parts.note: musing is thinking quietly

explanation.surface: Someone finds a joke on April Fool's Day funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusing describes something that causes laughter.

clue.text: Ring to get hold of me? in retrospect, it's a hindrance

indicators.note: looking back means the whole sequence is read from the end

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
to grab is to seize

explanation.surface: Phoning someone to get hold of them turns out, looking back, to be an obstacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retrospect' turns OGRABME round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban on trade, an obstacle placed in its way.

clue.text: Overblown border with flowers in columns

indicators.note: blown over suggests turning the word for border the other way round

parts.note: a lip is an edge or rim
asters are daisy-like flowers

explanation.surface: An overdone flowerbed edging stands among columns.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilasters are flat rectangular columns projecting from a wall.

clue.text: Charming rustic home improvements ruined by apprentice left in charge

indicators.note: spoilt, so those letters are rearranged

parts.note: DIY is do-it-yourself work on the home
L is a learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A trainee left in charge has botched the DIY at a pretty cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: Idyllic means peacefully pleasant, like an idealised countryside scene.

clue.text: Has shiny spots and sharp pain, having been run over by toboggan

indicators.note: the toboggan passes over the pain, so the pain ends up inside the sled

parts.note: a sled is a sledge or toboggan
a pang is a sudden stab of pain

explanation.surface: Someone run over by a toboggan has bruises and a sharp pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Spangled means decorated with glittering spots, sequin-like.

clue.text: Good opening line to incomplete article, for spread

indicators.note: the good letter comes at the start

parts.note: a row is a line

indicators.note: the article loses its last letter

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Advice on starting an unfinished piece of writing with a good line.
explanation.definitionFit: Growth and spread both mean increase or expansion.

clue.text: Article is made practical

indicators.note: made here means formed anew, so the letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece has been made sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: Realistic means sensible and down to earth, a synonym of practical.

clue.text: Worn by former premier coddling nasty cold?

definitions.text: Worn by former premier coddling nasty cold?

indicators.note: coddling means wrapping up, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: Edward Heath was British Prime Minister 1970-74

indicators.note: a nasty cold is a bad one, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ex-Prime Minister nursing a bad cold has wrapped up his head.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath was a 1970s British Prime Minister; 'nasty' jumbles the cold and 'coddling' wraps him round it, picturing him with his head covered.
explanation.definitionFit: A headcloth is a cloth worn over the head, as someone with a cold might wear one.

clue.text: Rigging used by sailor returning after a row

indicators.note: turning back, so the sailor's word is read backwards

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
a row is a line

explanation.surface: Ship's rigging used by a sailor coming back after an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratlines are the small ropes across a ship's shrouds forming ladders, part of the rigging.

clue.text: Father turned up with one of his ilk, it's understood

indicators.note: in a down clue this reads the word upwards, so backwards

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
a parent is of the same kind as a father

explanation.surface: Dad arrives with another of his sort, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means plain to see, clearly grasped.

clue.text: Be sparing in use of open-weave fabric from Peter's head

parts.note: scrim is a loosely woven cotton or linen fabric

indicators.note: the head of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone economises on loose-weave cloth from Peterhead.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text runs the words together; the clue needs 'Peter's head', the first letter of Peter.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to economise, to be frugal.

clue.text: The downfall of a barber

parts.note: a heavy fall, as in coming one, and also someone who crops hair

explanation.definitionFit: To come a cropper is to fall heavily; a barber crops hair.

clue.text: Coming out and is going to court, we hear

parts.note: taken as written
suing someone is taking them to court

explanation.surface: Someone is going public and also intends to sue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' is padding suggesting the words run together as one is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Issuing means emerging or being sent out.

clue.text: The rest, unfortunately, require permit to fish

indicators.note: unluckily placed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: to let is to allow

explanation.surface: The rest need a licence to go fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: The sterlet is a small sturgeon prized for caviar.

clue.text: Bizarre details about duck put in quarantine

indicators.note: around, so the jumble encloses the duck
strange, so these letters come out in a weird order

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, O

explanation.surface: Odd particulars about a duck placed in quarantine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bizarre' turns DETAILS into ISLATED, which goes 'about' O; a duck is a cricket score of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolated means kept apart from others, as in quarantine.

clue.text: Pipes from one vessel inside another

indicators.note: the first vessel goes within the second

parts.note: SS is a steamship, another kind of vessel
a ewer is a large jug

explanation.surface: Plumbing: one container sits inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewers are drainage pipes for waste.

clue.text: Lady of the lake'

definitions.meaning: belonging to the lake on the borders of Germany, Switzerland and Austria

explanation.definitionFit: Constance is both a girl's name and the English name of the Bodensee.

clue.text: Walter's dissipated — good for nothing!

indicators.note: scattered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Walter has wasted his life and is worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: A wastrel is an idle, worthless person.

clue.text: Spirits? See footnote about customs

indicators.note: turned about, so the footnote letters are read backwards

parts.note: PS is a postscript, an added note at the foot
rites are customary ceremonies

explanation.surface: A note about traditions is appended to a page on spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprites are elves or fairies, spirits of folklore.

clue.text: Design in torn clothing

indicators.note: the aim goes within the rip

parts.note: rent means ripped
an aim is an intention or design

explanation.surface: A pattern in ripped clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an archaic word for garments.

clue.text: Cows just seen in marshes

indicators.note: placed within the marshes

parts.note: fens are low marshy land in eastern England
right means just or fair

explanation.surface: Cattle spotted grazing in marshland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cows' looks like a noun but is the verb, intimidates.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to scare them into submission.
